quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Stop until the dog loses interest.
Ride alongside the dog.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear.
Use the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Push the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Push the handle grip opposite to the direction you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, push the left grip, then push the right to straighten. To swerve right, push the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When must a motorcycle's headlight be on?

options.text: Only at night.
At all times when riding.
Only when visibility is less than 25 feet.
Only in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times when riding.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. This is the easiest way to make sure other drivers see your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should your riding clothes NOT protect you from?

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. They should also protect you in a crash.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before slowing down to warn them.
Speed up.
Pull over to the side of the road.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before slowing down to warn them.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating. The tailgater may not notice hazards ahead that require slowing down.

questions.question: How do you get maximum straight-line braking?

options.text: Use the front brake, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum straight-line braking happens when you use both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Follow me
Slow down
Speed up
Exit

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
The person's body weight
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. Drinking and driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift to neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: What should you do when a vehicle is passing you from behind?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder.
Use the left side of your lane.
Use the center of your lane.
Use the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. This is the safest position. Riding on the side closer to the passing vehicle increases your risk of a collision. Riding on the far side can make the driver try to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before you hit it.
Slow down before you hit it.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you hit it.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease the throttle down just before impact. Try to hit the object at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the operator.
Behind the operator.
They do not need to reach the footrests.
They should hold onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child passenger should always ride behind the operator. A child in front may not balance properly and could block the operator's control of the motorcycle.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, wet or slippery roads make it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: What is true about rounded, convex mirrors on motorcycles?

options.text: They are easy to get used to right away.
They make cars look closer than they really are.
They provide a narrow view of the road.
They make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice judging distances in these mirrors if you are not used to them.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing your motorcycle?

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Ride alongside the dog.
Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Then accelerate and leave it behind. If a large animal is chasing you, brake and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed.
Body weight.
How fast the alcohol was consumed.
How often a person drinks alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol.
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have an effect.

questions.question: What should a rider do when entering a turn?

options.text: Speed up.
Reduce their speed.
Move their shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, reduce your speed by easing off the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign.
Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when it is warm outside while riding?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take breaks to remove it and cool down.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: In warm weather, a riding jacket helps prevent dehydration and protects you. Many jackets are designed to protect riders from overheating, even when it is warm.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Try to use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, do one action first, then the other. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: You should maintain a minimum following distance of two seconds. Increase this to at least three seconds when riding in bad weather or poor conditions.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give them?

options.text: Get on after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move unnecessarily to keep you focused on riding. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.
